title: The geometry of neural network decision boundaries
abstract: arXiv:2611.24557v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are built using well-understood mathematical operations, yet their complex nature poses significant challenges to intuitively understanding their decision-making processes. This work introduces a method for visualizing and measuring ANN decision boundary geometry directly in the high-dimensional input space, avoiding distortions found with traditional projection-based techniques. We analyze boundary curvatures and distances in diverse inputs, architectures, and training methods. Boundary distances grow smoothly and slowly with consistent curvature as the size of the subspace increases, suggesting that decision boundaries are close to input samples within large, continuous subspaces. We also quantify how much boundary distances and curvatures reduce near dataset samples after adversarial training. Training methodology has a significantly stronger impact on boundary distance and curvature than architecture

translated_title: 神经网络决策边界的几何学
translated_abstract: 人工神经网络（ANN）由人们充分理解的数学运算构建而成，但其复杂的特性给直观理解其决策过程带来了重大挑战。本研究提出了一种方法，可以直接在高维输入空间中可视化和测量ANN决策边界的几何形状，避免了传统基于投影技术的失真问题。我们分析了在不同输入、架构和训练方法下的边界曲率和距离。随着子空间规模的增大，边界距离平滑且缓慢地增长，同时保持一致的曲率，这表明决策边界在大而连续的子空间内接近输入样本。我们还量化了对抗训练后数据集样本附近边界距离和曲率的降低程度。研究还发现，训练方法对边界距离和曲率的影响显著强于架构的影响。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种直接在高维输入空间中可视化和测量神经网络决策边界几何形状的方法，揭示了决策边界在大连续子空间内接近输入样本，且训练方法对边界几何的影响显著大于网络架构。
